verificationPolicy.rule: A source is listed here ONLY if the URL was actually opened during verification, or its existence and metadata were returned by the publisher's own catalogue API.
acceptedVerificationMethods: fetch_page on the source URL and read returned content
archive.org advancedsearch API returning identifier + title + language + creator for that exact identifier
archive.org metadata API returning the item file list for that exact identifier
archive.org full-text derivative read (title page / index page)

verificationLevels.content-read: The page was opened and its content read - including, where noted, the printed text of a book reached through its full-text derivative. Sources carrying verifiedPassages may be cited down to a passage.
verificationLevels.metadata-verified: The item exists and its title/language/creator were returned by the catalogue API; the body text was not read page by page.
verificationLevels.catalogue-verified: A print-book listing (ISBN / publisher / page count) was confirmed on two independent bookseller catalogues. No free full text exists.
verificationLevels.linked-not-opened: The URL appears as a link inside a source that WAS opened, but it was not opened separately. Do not cite as an authority until opened.
verificationLevels.dead: URL was attempted and is unreachable. Listed only so nobody re-adds it.

guardrailTransforms._why: The two Tamil books read at passage level (TA-02, TA-07) were written in a register this product may not use: they name death, they name diseases, and they prescribe gold, silver images, goats and buffaloes. They are still the best Tamil remedy sources available, so the knowledge base stores the SOURCE text and the TRANSFORMED text side by side. The retrieval layer returns only the transformed text; the source text stays in the file so every citation is auditable.
dropEntirely: மரணம் / மிருத்யு / அகால மிருத்யு (death, untimely death) as a predicted outcome
any named disease: மாலைக்கண் நோய், காதில் நோய், நேத்திர ரோகம், வைசூரி, பித்த ரோகம்
invocation of the deity of death (மிருத்யு தேவதை ஆவாகனம்)
loss of wife or children phrased as a certainty
the word தோஷம் used as a threat rather than as a neutral technical term
guardrailTransforms.rewriteTo: a tendency, a period, and a practice - "X lord in the 8th can put pressure on money and standing; this usually eases as the Bhukti changes; here is a simple practice" - never "X will die / will lose his wife / will go blind".
